players.note: If Flowers didn't exit Week 1 early with a hamstring injury, it would already be too late to buy him. But that injury has perhaps opened one final window to acquire a guy who could be the story of the season. Flowers racked up five catches for 150 yards on just 11 routes on Sunday, absurd efficiency. He also hit pay dirt, already matching 20% of his total TD production from last season. This confirms my priors that Flowers is a truly elite talent who has just been unlucky on the touchdown front and is now primed for a monster year in Baltimore's new offense.

Normally, I prefer buying high after Week 1 rather than attempting to buy low, which is usually easier said than done. But Jaylen Waddle's Denver debut was so bad — one catch for two yards on just three targets — that his early-round investors may already be panicking. Denver's offense looked terrible all around on Monday night, but Waddle still led the team with a respectable 79% route share. More importantly, I simply believe in his talent eventually winning out. If you do too, now is the time to send an offer.

If you paid any attention to fantasy football discussions this offseason, you probably heard that Davante Adams' 2025 success was largely based on unique usage as the Rams' go-to goal-line offense. Although his numbers were otherwise down across the board, 14 touchdowns, 11 of which came from within the 10-yard line, carried his season. With this in mind, it's an absolutely massive red flag that Adams played just one of LA's nine snaps inside the 20-yard line in Melbourne. Nine snaps (only six of which were inside the 10) is a small sample, but given how TD-dependent Adams' profile is at this point, I'd recommend overreacting rather than underreacting to this change in usage.

Don't sell low on Luther Burden, who still has massive upside. Kalif Raymond isn't suddenly the Bears' WR1. However, it is undeniably concerning that Burden posted just a 68% route participation rate against the Panthers. With Rome Odunze dealing with a calf injury, that was actually the highest among Chicago's WRs, but it's far lower than we normally expect from starting wideouts, which is legitimately concerning. While everyone else argues about Colston Loveland's donut, try to quietly sell Burden at his draft-day cost, which he should fall from at least a little given what we just saw.

Jameson Williams' 2026 season debut was one to forget. He tied for the league lead with two drops and added a near-fumble on an end-around for good measure. But Jamo's actual role was elite: nine targets (23% share) and 128 air yards (56% share). As long as that usage continues, some huge fantasy days are in his future.

A couple of close calls meant it didn't show up in the box score, but DK Metcalf's role was excellent on Sunday. The veteran wideout racked up 194 air yards, the second most of any player in the league. He also ran more in-breaking routes than last year: 54% of his routes were in-breaking, up from just 34% in 2025. Meanwhile, the Steelers' offense as a whole was shockingly pass-happy. Put these facts together, and Metcalf should easily rebound from this relatively slow start going forward.

Downs' final Week 1 stat line — two receptions on four targets for 37 scoreless yards — was mediocre. But there's one encouraging number that should be far more predictive of his long-term results: route share. Downs led the Colts' offense with an 85% route share against Baltimore. That is higher than any single week he posted last year and 20% above his season average. Especially notably, Downs also stayed on the field for three of the Colts' five passing plays in one- or two-WR sets. If this keeps up, Downs' long track record of excellent per-route stats should come through to make him a solid weekly play.

Christian Watson posted the gaudy stat line, but Matthew Golden operated as the Packers' WR1 on Sunday. The second-year speedster led the team in route share (87%) and target share (26%), and he barely trailed Watson with a still-impressive 109 air yards. Especially given that the Packers' offense actually posted a positive pass-rate over expectation — a huge departure from Matt LaFleur's usual tendencies — Golden is poised to dominate as long as this usage continues.

Lemon recorded three catches NFL debut ... for negative five yards. The 20th-overall pick was used exclusively at the line of scrimmage against the Commanders, somehow posting a negative ADOT on his four targets. But he was also on the field far more than we might have expected, ranking second to DeVonta Smith with a very respectable 85% route rate. Given Lemon's exciting prospect profile, those routes should turn into actual downfield targets sooner rather than later. Combine that with the easy-button usage he already saw, and we could have a solid weekly starter by the time the season really gets going.

Given that he's on the Browns, it's hard to see how Denzel Boston's NFL debut could have gone better. He led the team in route share (90%), tied for the lead in target share (18%), and lapped the field in air yards share (58%). He finished with a solid fantasy day, too, although that was admittedly almost entirely thanks to a 46-yard touchdown in the smelliest of garbage time. There's a real chance Cleveland's overall ineptitude keeps Boston from ever emerging as a weekly starter, but I'll always recommend buying into a rookie flashing upside while they're still cheap.

The Chiefs' passing offense didn't accomplish much on Monday (not that they needed to), as Travis Kelce was the only player to record more than 20 receiving yards. But underneath the hood, Xavier Worthy operated as the team's top wideout. The speedster led or tied for team highs in route share (82%), target share (22%), and air yards share (39%). Even if we are in for a new-look, run-heavy Kansas City offense, being Patrick Mahomes' top option should eventually pay fantasy dividends for Worthy.

Pat Bryant was the only Broncos receiver who did anything at all on Monday night, catching four of a team-leading six targets for 42 yards. As a second-year breakout candidate, he's worth adding in all formats. But we have to keep expectations in check: Bryant was still the Broncos' clear WR3 in terms of routes, with an unusably low 58% participation rate. If someone in your league wants to buy the upside at a high price, take that deal.

Antonio Williams isn't likely to be startable any time soon — he only ran 11 routes on Sunday. But he racked up four targets on those 11 routes, catching all four for 64 yards and a TD. I wouldn't actually pay anything with real value to acquire the third-round rookie, but he's a must-add. It's better to be early than late when a young player is flashing target-earning ability, especially when they're on a potentially exciting offense with non-elite competition.

This one is simple. Jayden Reed's price was inflated this offseason because some fantasy managers were holding out hope that he would finally see real usage outside of three-WR sets. That didn't happen, as his four routes in heavier personnels were good for just a 24% participation rate. This translated to an overall participation rate of just 63% for the slot specialist, right in line with his career norms. This massively caps Reed's upside (again), making him a clear sell candidate.
